TL;DR this game is a very nice improvement over SGW3, focusing on quality of smaller areas (ditching open world from SGW3) over quantity. Some very minor downgrades and issues but overall I recommend it, more so than Contracts 2 to be honest as it takes what SGW3 did good, and builds upon it (while not truly open world, you can approach missions anyway you want), while not being too much of a downgrade (most of which are UI things and generally are super minor).

Sniper Ghost Warrior 3 was when the game series started to improve, however a major downside to SGW3 is that, despite being open world, enemies would despawn after a certain distance, leading to a very lackluster sniper experience since you'll be shooting from a distance within 300m most of the time with a few exceptions. SGWC1 (Contracts 1), remedied this by having the world semi-open world or at least what I would define as a semi-open world experience. You have 5 regions, within those regions are contracts/jobs, you do them, you get paid. You get additional money from challenges within that region (for example, kill only this guy and nobody else, get x amount of additional money), and collect bounties that are within the area. The nice thing about SGWC1 is that, once you've completed either one of the primary objectives and exfil, you can continue on, or quit, and restart the mission and repeat that part to farm money. Same goes with challenges, you can complete an area in segments, or do it one single shot, then later on you can revisit the mission and complete any challenges you missed, while still getting money from completing the main contracts. This is not present in SGWC2 (Contracts 2), once you complete a main mission in C2, you CAN replay it, but you DO NOT get money for replaying it. If you make a purchase you regret in C2, you're stuck with it as the game won't give you the reward money for replaying contracts.

While its an overall improvement of SGW3 which IMO is still a decent game (just not quite good enough due to enemy despawn distance being so low), there are some minor downgrades, most of which are in the HUD/UI. For starters, your minimap is garbage. It just gives you dots which doesn't show which way the enemy is facing, a little too simple IMO, it works but its not great. C2 eventually fixes that. The game does not have the SGW aiming dot that helps with wind/bullet drop compensation, not the end of the world, makes for a more fun and challenging game, but if you need that assistance, sadly its not present in C1, it gets brought back in C2. There are minor things that should've been displayed on the HUD, but aren't until SGWC2. Thermal vision is infinite use on your mask. but regular mask/highlight mode isn't, but you don't have a battery indicator on screen until SGWC2 so you have no idea how much power your mask has until it can't use "highlight" mode. You can only tag enemies in mask/scout mode, that is also THE ONLY WAY to range a target. Your fancy scope DOES NOT have a range finder that gives you the exact range. You only have the range estimation lines where you line up the top of the target's head to the line. So if you see a target show up while scoped in, and they aren't tagged, you either need to use the range-estimation lines, or just know your holds/have mental distance markers/references because you're going in blind since if you're using a bipod for example, you can't use mask mode unless you stop using bipod, not just unscoping, but specifically leaving bipod mode/not bracing up against cover for stability.

Another major downgrade I've noted is that you can't retrieve C4 or decoy traps. If you place a block of C4, or a decoy trap, you can't get it back. Not only is there no "Press E" prompt, just pressing and holding it does nothing. I know some items don't show the prompt, for example the Motion Sensors/Warning Devices, if you place those down, you don't get a prompt, but you can still retrieve them by facing them and holding "E". Why this is a thing I don't know. This issue of not showing prompts is also present with ledge climbing, most ledges are highlight showing you can grab/climb them. Carried over for SGW3. However there are some ledges that aren't highlighted at all, but CAN be grabbed/climbed. Sometimes the highlight is covered by stuff but there are plenty of ledges you'll come across where you go into "Mask mode" and it won't show up, but you absolutely CAN grab onto said ledge.

One of the more major issues I've had with the game is jumping/movement and getting stuck. Seems kinda vague but let me explain. Sometimes you go over a surface and it seemed fine at first, but now you're stuck. Just stuck. Unable to move, crouch, jump, whatever. You're stuck, just floating there. Sometimes you jump over a rock or something, you land and next thing you know, you're stuck, can't move at all, can't jump, crouch, prone, etc. What is the fix? Die, or restart from a checkpoint. This is a very big issue that happens way too often, I'm honestly terrified to run around and jump in certain terrain because of the possibility that I might get stuck and since one of the challenges for a certain region is to complete ALL contracts without loading a single checkpoint, one accidental misstep that you couldn't have possibly anticipated, could cause you to get stuck for good, forcing you to restart from the beginning of the mission.

Aside from some of the fairly minor issues listed above (most of which being UI issues/downgrades), overall I recommend this game even over SGWC2. That game despite being newer and being the successor to C1, has just as many issues (if not more) and downgrades FROM C1 which will be listed off when I eventually beat that game and write a review for it. Unlike C2 and SGW3, this game feels finished and polished. SGW3 and especially SGWC2, feel VERY unpolished and in some aspects quite disappointing since its supposed to be newer which generally means its supposed to improve from its predecessors.

Fun, but bug-ridden. The game is also relatively short with only 5 maps (containing several quick objectives per map). Worth it on sale if you like either Sniper Elite or using snipers in the Far Cry series. Full price is $6 per mission which is too much imo.

What stands out about this game is the movement feels more like Far Cry while the sniping is more "realistic" like Sniper Elite, making a good blend of the two games.

I would highly recommend the game, but bugs such as freezing on launch, not saving resolution between launches, textures not loading in (including entire walls), missing audio queues, extra audio queues, and invisible enemy awareness warnings make me hesitant to recommend to anyone that hasn't played a similar game before.

Like others have said the autosave is honestly random. Not only is it on a random timer, it also wont save in the same place. Ex: walked up a safe stairwell and it saved... 20 minutes later I walked down the same stairwell, it didn't save, then I glitched through the floor and died. Causing me to have to replay that entire segment. It'll also, very occasionally, save in the middle of combat. Where if you die and respawn the dead bodies will disappear and you'll be in the middle of the enemy base with no guards alerted.

The story is serviceable. It takes major inspiration from the Hitman games by IO Interactive. However, there is no reason for the player to care. Throughout the story you are told "don't worry about it, it's just a contract" then at the end the narrator/handler spills the beans to you in one exposition dump that he has no reason to share with the player.

Then there are half-baked gameplay mechanics that are just disappointing once you notice them. You are prompted to interrogate one target to get the location of another. This is difficult to do since you must get close to him in the middle of his guards without alerting anyone. He then refuses to tell the player the location and you are forced to kill him anyways.... not that any of it mattered because the location of the other target has been marked on your map since the beginning of the mission.

Another mechanic is that about halfway though the missions you start entering the map right next to a group of enemies and have to fight or sneak your way through them with almost no room to maneuver or retreat... but once again your map has the solution. Just open it up and select a location to fast-travel to. Usually there is a spot just past the group of enemies, or you can go across the whole map if you want. Making these fast travel locations unlockable by visiting them would fix this.

Difficulty is also slightly too easy after a while. The enemies don't get harder to fight as you go through levels, there's just more of them grouped up together. I played on the hardest difficulty / did not upgrade skills or guns and there were still a few things I wish I could turn up the difficulty on: 
[*]On hard (Deadeye) enemies still have pretty small cones of vision unless they are snipers or using binoculars. I wish there was an option to give them the same vision that they have when "alerted". I would occasionally alert on purpose just to have a bit of a challenge, but they also run around and hide in this mode which is (understandably) annoying to deal with. 
[*]The wind bullet drop is always shown on the GUI. I don't think this should be turned off by higher difficulty, but I would like to see an option for it in the Gameplay Settings menu. (while still showing wind speed & direction at the top of the HUD)
[*]Most sniper engagements (99%) happen at 50m-250m, it's really hard to find a line of sight to let you snipe further than this. I upgraded my gun after beating the game to just compare and I found that there is no reason to; the fact that the upgraded reticles go up to 2500m is a joke. The zoom on the original sniper is more than enough to get easy headshots every time.
[*]Skill upgrades and level difficulty don't seem to correlate much. Most of the useful upgrades appear to be for people who can't snipe effectively. I found these to address most of the issues I ran in to when using a controller (Steam Deck) such as not being able to switch between two targets quickly (sniper turret), not being able to see clearly at long range (mask zoom upgrade & camera drone). But the vast majority address issues I can't imagine most people face such as better camo (bushes already make you 100% invisible if more than 10m away), more grenades (you're doing something wrong if you're going through more than 9 grenades before looting bodies), wall hacks (x-ray vision is a sign of the times when this game was developed), and armor upgrades.

I feel like I've complained a lot about my gripes in this game, but I do truly appreciate the multi-objective maps that allow you to approach from multiple angles. It's exactly what I was looking for in a game when I stumbled across this one.

TL;DR: Fun, medium-length game with little sense of progression both in story and in player development. Maps feel like they could be swapped around in any order so if you find you like it after getting through one of the docks in the second level keep playing, but if not go ahead and refund as you won't find anything different in later levels.

The game itself is pretty good. It gives enough variety for the player to try each mission in different strategies. You have plenty of sniper rifles to choose from, the rifles are rarely used, unless you're really bad at stealth and want to just to go loud all the time, and the pistols are quite questionable, since there are only 2-3 of them that have silencers. The missions themselves are pretty good too, each one having different scenarios that force you to adapt to different situations.
I also like the dynamics in each mission: the fact you can fast travel, different instances that do not interact with each other when one is alerted, unique bounty targets, collectibles which give a nice spice to the lore of game.

The only thing that I am really annoyed about this game, is that there are lots of tiny bugs that ruin the experience. Being a game developer myself, I noticed at least 10 bugs, and another one at the clip after the last mission (I ain't going to spoil it, since it's pretty noticeable. I'm warning you, once you see it, you cannot un-see it).
Here are a few of the bugs that I have noticed, and I hope that the team will maybe do something about it (or hire me to fix them, who knows, LOL):
- Body slamming a guard while being a drone will somehow kill the guard and tackle you to the ground for no reason
- Hacked turrets can sometimes still detect you, but won't shoot you
- Interrogating bounty targets can sometimes give you a basic dialogue instead of the unique dialogue assigned for each bounty target in this game (like the one that you have when you interrogate a normal guard)
- The sniping turret sometimes just doesn't correctly shoot the target, despite being at a short range, which is EXTREMELY ANNOYING, since the gadget is theoretically supposed to give you an edge in each mission
- Shooting certain parts of vehicles that make them explode don't actually explode unless you're in a specific range, which is also very questionable
- Some animations in the second mission when you're planting the explosives are just... weird. It's non-fluid, it feels like something it's supposed to happen, but nothing is happening
... and many other bugs that I have discovered in my first 50 hours of playing.

I don't know if I'm being too critical or if those bugs are too noticeable. It feels like the developers have rushed to get the final touches done but instead they managed to mess the game up.

Overall, the game is good. It's got potential, you do feel like a cool sniper hired by some anonymous group that assigns you different contracts to assasinate, you have variety in play style, and you can make some sick plays if you really want to show off on YouTube LOL.
It's a shame that when spending a few hours in the game you'll notice the bugs and ruin the game experience,

a great bridge between arcade tactical FPS, sniping simulator and stealth immersive sim, SGW:C puts you in the shoes of a mask-wearing goon by the name of seeker, who is tasked by a shadowy organisation to eliminate targets and perform key objectives across several sites located in siberia; ranging from snowstorm-ridden mountains to luxury forest estates to remote arctic islands and more.

 each area drops you in and has a list of key objectives you must complete in any order, mainly consisting of several assassination targets and a couple of intel-gathering/sabotage tasks; in classic im-sim fashion the maps are open-ended aside from the odd bottleneck in certain areas with many ways to proceed and eliminate your targets. do you wanna find a nice bush on a hill and wait for the perfect moment to deliver a half-mile sniper shot, do you wanna go chaotic-stealth and dive in with explosives and silenced automatics? do you wanna go full ninja mode, quietly plant a C4 by the target and blow 'em up from across the map while you wait by the exfil point? you can do all of those, provided the AI is generous enough to not look in your direction.

 Enemies are responsive and behave accordingly, taking cover and charging your position in a co-ordinated fashion; enemies' awareness is highly dependent on light level and atmospheric conditions; in a snowstorm you're nigh invisible, but on a calm sunny day there's a chance you'll get spotted from ways off, which can turn a routine stroll into a hectic game of katyn mouse when a whole squad of enemy snipers decides to clock you while you sneak through the middle of a valley.

 If you're here for story, maybe don't look too closely. The majority of the plot is deferred, meaning you'll only really get the picture if you go out of your way to interrogate your contract targets and grab collectible items, and even then there's not a lot to it.

This game has a serious identity crisis.
It can't figure out if it wants to be a tactical sniper or stealth based assassination type game.

For me, I rather enjoyed Sniper 3. 
The developers stated they were over-ambitious and didn't have the time, resources, or money to complete their goal. Personally, I would have rather them continue with the larger maps than switch to the smaller linear style game play of 'Sniper Contracts'.

At least in the previous game you felt a need to use a rifle due to the massive layout of the world. With this game, I feel a high powered AR with an ACOG scope would be just as effective. There were points in the game where I would just sneak into a base with my silenced pistol and take down everyone.

Which brings me back to my point... This game has a serious identity crisis! 

Having played 'Sniper 3' I knew this really wasn't a tactical sniper game and for me that's perfectly fine.
But if this is going to be the future of the series moving forward, I would much rather them call the entire game 'CONTRACTS' and say "here are a bunch of weapons/gear choose what you want to complete the missions" over forcing me to use a sniper rifle (as a  primary weapon) on a tiny map, just so they can call the game 'Sniper Something'.

So developers, please choose what type of game you want to make...

If you want to be a sniper game, you need to rethink your clustered environment and add some more realistic ballistic properties. If you want to be a stealth game (Hitman/Splinter Cell), vary the weapons/tactical gear and let me choose what I want for each mission. There are many mission related bugs - some objectives cannot be completed, some suddenly fail while I am on the other side of the map. Where's the fun in identifying and eliminating the correct target, when the double then just dies at some point later, whithout me having part in it?

Save points are frustrating. They seem random, and resetting to one might change the setup around it - enemies suddenly being gone or somewhere else. Situations and targets might be changed according to actions you took after saving - you reach a checkpoint, do some scouting, mess up, the targets retreat - you load the checkpoint, need to do the scouting again, and find out the targets have already gone to cover, reacting to the "undone" action before loading again. Soemtimes I'd die due to the mentioned takedown-problem, and restart at a completely different part of the level, although seeing the save-icon shortly before dying.

When spotted by enemies - which sometimes happens way too easily, sometimes you wonder whether they're blind and dumb - they will hit you with their iron-sighted assault rifles at distances you and your sniper rifle would struggle without 16x zoom and wind adjustment.

You can't see what attachments and special rounds a weapon can use before buying it - resulting in you only finding out after you've bought them that some snipers, none of the secondary weapons and the ingame Glock can not equip suppressors.

Thee is no proper cover-mechanic - in a stealth game, you'd imagine you could hide behind boxes and other hip-high objects, but you can't - crouch up to them as close as possible, you still might be seen, and there is no "hiding" action.

Spotting enemies with the binocular mode if the mask is easily thrown off by railings, fences, and similar objects - the face of the enemy clearly visible, but you can't mark them because they are behind a railing. In general it fells, with merking and moving, as if the real limits and borders of objects do not match the ingame-texture and model, sometimes featuring a bigger size or surface than you can actually see.

This nearly defeats the point of stealth or trying to be stealth as I just found myself killing guards because it seemed like sneaking around they would spot me anyways. There were even times I was laying in the tall grass behind a group and was spotted even though their backs were turned to me. I feel that this issue destroys the idea of being stealthy and sneaking past pointless fights as it just lead to me killing groups just to progress anyways.

2. The combat.

 Yes I know the game is primarily a stealth sniper game but there are times you're forced or dropped into a fire fight that you have to use your secondary weapons to handle it. I found the secondary weapons clunky and just about as useless as the sniper rifle at times. Weapons either had a sudden and uncontrollable kick or just felt completely ineffective at doing anything to an enemy while they could dispatch you just by looking at you. Combat in itself feels clunky and awkward as you feel like you're moving around in a big heavy suit and you have to make deliberate actions in order to move or fire back in combat. It feels more like an after thought than something that was intended in the game. It also seems like hit boxes are not matched up with the character models when you shoot at them. There are times my shots though looked dead on would pass through a target's head or right through them leading to me getting spotted and killed.

3. Key mapping.

   Isn't much to really say but a serious lack of being able to remap keys and functions just are something I don't like and I find myself hitting the wrong keys for certain functions just because I know for other games it's how I would've had them set for.

4. Frame drops


  Now I don't know if this is just me or anyone else is dealing with this but I do get times where I will be at about 60 or so fps and then it will spike down to 5 at random times. It has caused me to screw up shots or over step out of cover and get spotted. Not sure though but this could just be something on my end that could be an issue and not the game itself but I felt it was worth noting.


  Now I'm not saying I would not recommend because I want to blast this game but I know for many this isn't going to be the game for them. And with glaring issues I've dealt with while playing I know many are going to be frustrated through playing it. Finding myself going through missions with a lot of trail and error due to AI spotting me in areas that they couldn't have seen me in etc. As for the level design, visuals, voice acting, and the like I have no issue with it. Just the gameplay with dealing with enemies and the like are well... they need work and I do know the dev team is working on it and i hope as time goes on it gets its kinks worked out. But as for what it stands right now I can't recommend this game to others at it's current state. Perhaps later down the line that will change but for now I really can't do that.

[u] Positive points: [/u]

    [*]Bullet cam is decent, heads explode in an amusing way

    [*]Decent cinematics and voice acting

[u] Negative points: [/u]

[list]
    [*]Absurd level design. Complex paths and tall grass everywhere but very few places to actually snipe from. Sight lines are very limited so you have to kill more than 50% of enemies with a suppressed pistol if you want to stay in stealth. The level design combined with enemy placement means that it is impossible to kill most enemies with a sniper rifle without being seen. The level design funnels you into close combat and the interrogation mechanic encourages you to get close to an enemy which is stupid. Just far too many pathways and not enough open space to actually get to use your sniper rifle.

    [*]Takedowns from behind are noisy and alert other enemies

    [*]AI is baffling. When they notice they're being shot at they just hide behind cover doing nothing. Sometimes they send an armored vehicle towards you but it can bug out. They're also ridiculously accurate with their assault rifles at almost any range. Sometimes they're dumb idiots and sometimes complete gods.

To give an example: 

 I set down a poison mine along the route of a patrolling pair of soldiers and then retraced my steps to a known location to look for a vantage point so I could shoot towards the facility. When the enemy died to the poison mine, the entire base sounded an alarm. Slightly bizarre since the soldiers were not in direct view and there was no one close to where the mine was. At this point I was 300-400 meters away from the facility and somehow the enemy knew where I was. And I was being shot at. I tried to look with the binoculars to find what was shooting at me. Once their aggression reaches a certain state it seems that as long as they have a direct sight line to you, they are able to shoot you accurately no matter how far away you are. 


    [*]Checkpoint save system means you could potentially lose huge progress. At one point I loaded into a checkpoint inside of a hut and the enemy commander that I had killed earlier was respawned. 

    [*]Your own traps are lethal against you and you can trigger them yourself. Completely stupid and discourages their use because for example if you cover your rear with a mine you could forget about it and later on step on it and die immediately, potentially losing huge progress because of checkpoint save.

    [*]More of a subjective point but the character's blocky/polygon looking mask looks silly

Pros:

2- The free-form objectives system is interesting.  Though the levels feel a little too closed-in for it to feel sandboxy.

Anyways... it feels like the team that was working on game mechanics might have said something that upset the team that did the environment design.  Because the latter almost feels purpose-built to sabotage the former.

This games somehow has worse stealth mechanics than Splinter Cell: Blacklist and MGSV. How, I have no idea, but even for $5 this game isnt worth it.

-First and foremost, no manual save system is absolutely crazy for a game released in 2019.

-Poor PC optimization. Just standing around makes my FPS fluctuate, and this game *should* run well on my 3060.

-No options for silenced secondary weapons.

-Player character gets caught on every single little piece of protruding geometry, which becomes infuriating after the 5th time it happens.

-If you accidentally get discovered, even if you kill the enemy who sees you without them firing a shot, everyone on base immediately knows where you are despite the person that discovered you not making any broadcasts to others or tripping an alarm.

-Movement feels sluggish as all hell. Like, I get it, a "Ghost Warrior" cant just be running and gunning, this isnt Call of Duty, but it just feels horrible, cumbersome, and slow.

-No elevation on objective markers. Oh, there is a place where you can see a collectible or plant some c4? No way to tell on the map if its above of below you. Also, there isnt any way I can find to manually place a marker on the map. Which wouldnt really matter if you could, because the game doesnt have a compass, somehow. (???)

-Inconsistent bullet trajectories, which is awful considering that that should be the 100% most well detailed part of a SNIPING GAME. Even when no wind is present, bullets can sometimes veer off left or right midflight, which you cant correct for.

-The bug in this game are everywhere. Planting explosives or doing other things sometimes renders you as unable to hold a gun, you have to use the radial menu rather than the hotkey to switch weapons, which can get you killed at the wrong time. Wind sometimes instantly changes from one direction to another, instead of doing so gradually. Sometimes wind will just be blowing while youre indoors, affecting your shots somehow. Enemies looking for you with binoculars will sometimes give you a warning to get to cover, other times will just pick you up instantly with no chance to hide. Sniper rifle damage is also inconsistent, I had single shot kills to the chest on some basic enemies, but not others, while using the same rifle.

-A total lack of gun customization. Maybe its because I only played for 4 hours, but I only had a single Sniper Rifle and pistol that had a suppressor on it. You cant manually add a suppressor to any rifle. In a game that makes you calculate distance and wind speed/direction and adjust your rifle sights accordingly, why cant I choose to put a silencer on whatever gun I want? Also, for being a sniping sim, why are suppressors unlimited use?

-Enemies are FAR too accurate.. A soldier with an AK landing 6 shots on me from 250+ meters away is insane, especially when the designated counter-snipers the enemy has have to take time to aim and shoot.

-Minor gripe, but the markers you tag enemies with are way too hard to see. White markers against a snowy environment is needlessly annoying to keep track of.

Do not buy this game for any price. You WILL be let down.

Do you want to relive the joys of Action Man comics you read when you were 5? The plot of Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts is for you! Join the devoted fandom, including all 45% of people who actually completed the first mission, according to achievements. Enjoy infinite replayability as the borked checkpoint system forces you to go back through areas you cleared out entirely before you were suddenly sniped by a black spot half a kilometer away! Live the thrill of starting missions from scratch when you inevitably hit "restart mission" instead of "restart from checkpoint" for the third time, because the menu has both tabs right next to each other.

Challenge yourself with in game additional tasks that push you past the bounds of what you feel you can accomplish and, indeed, what the developers can reasonably expect anybody to achieve with the moveset and ruleset afforded to you. I particularly love how these challenges contradict each other, with "kill the target from 300 metres away" and "complete the mission using only a knife" being afforded to you in the same mission. This brilliant decision gives you an opportunity to further appreciate the boring levels as you trudge through them multiple times to get the completion above 50%. 

I love how you can sometimes spend ages scouring the map to find your target, only to find that they haven't spawned in yet. It gives you ample time to appreciate the clumsy movement system, invisible walls, and climbing mechanics that will fail and drop you to your death as often as they work. Once, a target spawned right behind me inside a cloud of red smoke and gunned me down before I could even spot him. This was an incredible display of this game's incredible AI which, apart from this spot of physics-defying genius, largely involved ignoring me as I shoot their comrade in the head mid conversation, and they stand there gawking for several seconds waiting for their turn. Sometimes, I can crouch walk right through their line of sight without issue and other times I find them suddenly spotting me from across the map without warning and alerting the entire base.

Fourthly, mines travel like 2 cm when thrown, which means you basically must be directly on the spot in order to set mine, which means that if you enjoy trapping you'll often end up screwing yourself because you cannot disarm it when backtracking or even mark its location. Enemies also rarely send units to investigate when you're detected and instead just hide behind cover for all eternity. Meaning less chance your traps get triggered. 

Finally, Bounties tend to be right in your exfil location so quite often you'd end up activating the mission just as you wish to end your gaming session by approaching the exfil. This happened once while falling towards an enemy to do a death-from-above, in the time it took me to fall on top of him, he had turned around, seen me, and drew his weapon.
- There are no [i] meaningful [/i] stealth detection mechanics, just what level of crouched are you, and are you "concealed" in some foliage. One of the best moments I experienced in this game was being prone in some foliage with two enemies stopping to have a conversation almost right on top of me. Only to be immediately spotted a few seconds later by an enemy almost 70 meters away. Splinter Cell had dynamic light based sneaking figured out in 2002. - It plays very much like Far Cry 3. Most of my gameplay loop was throwing a rock to distract an enemy, sneaking behind him, watching the kill animation, and hiding the body. You can tell that the developers wanted to go with a sniper style Hitman with separate multi objective large maps that could give a lot of freedom in how you approach any given objective. You can replay each map and redo objectives for additional money and to complete challenges Unfortunately, while the game is packed with loads of different systems and aspects, not one of them works without something wrong with it.

The AI: The AI has two modes. The first mode is "off", where the enemies path around oblivious where you can walk up behind them without even crouching and they are totally oblivious. The second mode is psychic super soldier. The instant a single enemy sees you, every enemy within the encounter area is instantly not only aware of you, but your exact position. The standard grunts are immediately able to drill you with assault rifles without optics on full auto fire from more than 200 meters. you have to run and put a solid object between you and them or your life will drop and you will die in seconds.

Occasionally, you will have an enemy shooting at you with the sound of his full auto fire being decentralized so you can't even tell where it is coming from so it becomes impossible to shoot back. If you stop firing and relocate in a way that no enemies can see you, you have about a 50% chance that they still no where you are.

The animations: All animations are ponderously slow, cumbersome, and un-interruptable. Your character, supposedly a highly skilled assassin and infiltration specialist, re-chambers his bolt action rifle slower than a weekend shooter at a shooting range. Not at all like someone that is even remotely familiar with his weapon. This is likely done to add an arbitrary rate of fire to a bolt action gun but it feels sluggish and gets in the way.

Other animations like climbing, stealth takedowns, using devices, etc. all feel like they are being ponderously done by someone with no sense of urgency. They can not be interrupted and while they won't always get you killed, it will happen occasionally. You don't seem to care that someone walked in and started shooting you while you were slowly pulling out your smart phone, dusting it off, checking the screen, pointing it at a CCTV control box, then deciding to proceed with the process while still getting shot.

The weapons: All of the sniper rifles feel basically identical. The only difference is that the larger caliber guns can remove arms and legs. Other than that, they are basically reskins. The exception is the .308 semi automatic sniper rifle (I should note that it fires "fast" in the way that it shoots as fast as a bolt action in Sniper Elite or Battlefield) that actually feels usable.

The pistols feel weak, their only use is that they are able to be suppressed and since you are unable to fire your sniper rifle without looking through the scope, they are your only option for quietly killing someone at closer ranges.

Assault rifles are pointless in a lot of ways because you can't suppress them. You can only put an optic and the standard two magazine types. More bullets or faster reload. 

The whole thing feels rushed and like it was either untested, or the developers just didn't care to make sure that it played well.

Other points:
 
The menus are un-intuitive and cumbersome.

You can complete a portion of the bounties in a map and reach an "exfiltration point" where you upload the "data" on what you just did to your corporate masters (though, why the hell this is a thing is beyond me. You are specifically told that your "handler", cleverly named "Handler", has a live feed from your mask so he can see everything you do.) but you can't leave the map to spend any of the money that you just earned. Just made enough for a new gun, thermal vision, special ammunition slot, or drone upgrade and you want to buy it? Well, screw you. you have to start the entire map over if you want to buy it.

A personal gripe: There are no pickups or collectibles in the maps. These huge areas have absolutely no point once you kill your target or steel his diary from a trash can or whatever. All you need to do is a google image search for the word gun and you could have added tons of in-map pick up only, unpurchaseable guns to add to your collection but no, You can buy five of the same assault rifle or some new sniper rifles whose only difference from the others is that they may not be able to be suppressed. 

TLDR: Save this one for a VERY deep sale on a weekend where you have nothing to do or in the highly unlikely event of a rework by the developers. Out of the bag I want to say the story presents itself in such a way that it is only loosely held together by a single concept: Libération! 

You are "Seeker". From what I gather you are a mercenary hitman who has been used all over the world by various groups and people to do the dirty as it were. You are hired 
by a group and given a "Handler" and a mask. You are paid a nice fee and for lack of a better phrase told "See all these bad people, here is why they are bad... do your thing." 

Simple stuff. Now when I say: [b]But wait.. there's more![/b] I am sure you have a few ideas as to what this is. 
It's cliché. I do not want to give it all away here but if you think something smells off - You can guess the end of this game easily.

You go through Siberia and take out various targets within a corrupt government. Each and every one of these people are depicted as despicable. All bar the 
Eugenics doctor. She's doing some good... but for bad people. Pretty sure we could convert her. 

Either way - Bad people. omelettes, eggs and all that jazz. Each individual contract has their own thing and some of the information you can get from some "secondary" objectives 
can give you some info on what you are actually in for: Bulletproof Glass, particular quirks for ID, potential meetings and the such. Good to know what you are looking for and for 
that I do commend CIGames for rewarding the side missions on each map.

Overall however the story is very "one note", disjointed and short. If I didn't have a death count in the triple digits I doubt I would have spent 9 hours playing this game.

In my opinion: The story is as basic as a Nickelback song and as predictable as death is inevitable. Compound this with some good ole' sequel/DLC bait.
Left a bad taste in my mouth and I've tried marmite.

[H1]Mechanics[/h1]

The mechanics of this game are very similar to the Sniper Elite series - The higher the difficulty the more you need to work for each kill. Take out cameras so you don't get spotted, adjust elevation and wind speed, tag the targets, hold your breath, fire. 

I recommend a suppressor so you don't alert everyone and their cat within a 10 mile radius. These guns are meaty. Excellent sound design on this part.

The selection of bullets as well - oh my. Straight up decapitations and dismemberment, and the slow motion. Perfect chaos. We got .50 Cal bullets, luring rounds and even "Easy Mode" rounds - Make aiming a thing of the past.

If you ever played the previous game however this is all standard. The only difference is you now must do the side challenges of the contracts in order to upgrade 
Seeker to hold and use these bullets.

Each missions has a few side challenges that unlock tokens used to unlock particular skills. Each skill helps in one way or another and each tree has a split choice for perks. You can only have 1 of the 2, example: More Stamina [b]OR[/b] Faster stamina regeneration? That's smart.

The idea of the as a gameplay mechanic was a very good choice. The mask is the communication device as well as the HUD. All of the things you need are 
essentially built into the mask: Map, Binoculars, Thermal Vision & objective tracker - Think the MGS4 Eye Patch. The most useful Milti-tool you never think of.

I do miss the cars and all other travel equipment however - the 5 (Yes count that, 5) contracts in this game are vast and you die fast. Compound this with the autosave function 
that can just set you back a good 10 minute journey. Seeker can skip leg day for some time.

The cutscenes between each mission - your brief if you were so inclined - are some of the most beautiful cutscenes I have ever saw. Loved the style. I will say however that 
more work was clearly put into handler than Seeker as every line delivered by Seeker was laughable.

If you had been a silent protagonist I would have been happy but no... 
had to give him the most SyFy, B-Movie, Direct to DVD voice ever.

You also handle pretty bad. It takes a special breed of idiot to fall through the gap in some stairs because you slipped on solid, dry concrete in the sun. Every movement is 
like walking on bananas. 

I could understand this in the snow areas... not so much in the middle of a road when there is no snow... or ice... or bananas. Add on to this that when you come out of ADS it takes a week to turn in any direction. It's almost like you are in disbelief that you looked down the scope. 

The AI By the way... they will zero right in on you but they are as dumb as bricks any other time. Unless you shoot near them, shoot at them or they [b]somehow[/b] manage to see you - they are pitiful.

Mechanically - This game is almost solid. Clearly this game is built for multiple playthroughs but I could not bring myself to do it. The minefields man... PTSD. Add on to this 
all the points above and you can find a balance. 

[h1]Performance[/h1]

As stated earlier I streamed this game on the [b]HIGH[/b] preset and I got a solid 70+ FPS with some minor jitters. My biggest concern though? It's 2019... Why no Borderless 
window in the settings? Half-Life 2 has Borderless!

I suffered twice the game crashing to desktop - Call it "Launch Week Issues", benefit of the doubt there. Overall this game ran well... better than the previous instalment. 
I literally have nothing else to say about the performance. Absolute Dream

[h1]Overall[/h1]

Overall this game is as interesting as ready salted crisps. There is potential in there and many other interesting things can be done - but on it's own it's basic, uninteresting 
and boring. 

The highlight of playing this game was being 2nd on the Twitch page for this game. This game is better than SGW3 but to be fair it's not hard to improve on garbage. 

This game however - in my personal opinion - is just nicer smelling garbage. Many good improvements and kudos on that. Hands up - I liked them, yet this game still has some issues that plagued the previous game - Simple gameplay loop, terrible AI, boring and predictable story.

While the game looks decently polished on the surface, there's a myriad of issues below the surface that will grind gameplay to a halt consistently. Here's a few that I've encountered:

- There's no info available about the game. Seriously. With other games you have wikis, subreddits, guides and other resources if you need answers to trivial questions like "where do heavy soldiers take damage", but with this game there's absolutely nothing. Your only methods of getting any info are to either have a friend that knows about the game, or ask on the Steam discussion board and hope someone answers.

- To make the previous point even worse, the game doesn't explain anything but the bare bones of the mechanics. It will show you how to climb ledges with a 20 second segment and never mention it again. It will "teach" you about special ammo types by simply giving you the ammo, letting you shoot at targets and guess what the ammo does. It will straight up not tell you anything about the drone, which will probably confuse the hell out of you when you try to use it ingame and have it break instantly every time, only to hear from a friend that it's because there's indestructable jammer towers all over the place that aren't marked out or mentioned anywhere.

- The game is called "Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts" yet the mechanics actively discourage a sniper playstyle. The aforementioned jammer towers prevent you from gathering intel from afar using the drone, so it's very likely that you wont spot a soldier sitting behind a wall or building who will then get alerted. The guards rarely if ever walk out of sight of eachother without being lured away by rocks thrown by the player. And all of the side objective sniping targets require you to go loot the body after the kill. Why make a sniping game that forces you not to snipe? The most egregious discouragement is that one of the gadgets is an automated sniper turret, which you can simply mark targets for and it will shoot them for you. Indeed, why bother doing that one titular thing the game sets out to do, when you can simply let a 100% accurate AI turret do it for you?

- The only way to save the game is with checkpoints, which are rare and can't be revisited, which can lead to lost progress. My tally is 1,5 hours of lost progress out of the 6 hours I've played so far.

- The game may or may not arbitrarily randomize the enemies every time you load to a checkpoint. It doesn't matter if it's because you shut the game off, or if you died.

- The game makes a big deal about exfiltrating out of the mission after each objective is completed, but won't actually let you change the mission or your loadout unless you give up all of your progress in the mission. The game saves separately from the exfiltrations as well, so they serve absolutely no purpose.

I wish we had a 1-5 star rating system instead of a simple yes or no recommendation.  I hate your needing to fully recommend it or fully condemn a game with no middle ground.  It isn’t that simple.  This game has some really good parts, but to me, the bad parts are pretty significant hurdles to get over.

The aiming system on the sniper rifle is just awful and a significant step backwards from this games previous iteration. It’s very clunky and nearly impossible to use accurately at times.  The way Ghost Warrior 3 did it was way better.  Different isn’t always better.

To me, and this is a huge flaw, I hate that you are forced to use full automatic when using your assault rifle.  I’m a former Marine.  On only the rarest of occasions would you ever use this fire select mode as it’s inaccurate and a great waste of the limited ammunition you are provided.  Single shot is way better.  It’s way more accurate.  It’s way less wasteful and it’s less noisy.  A surgical one shot kill is almost always going to be better than spraying and praying.  This is the only first person shooter I’ve ever played that doesn’t offer you a fire select mode.  I realize that this is more of a Hitman, slow and stealthy shooter and not an aggressive run and gun FPS, but there will always be players that want to play a little less stealthy and use their assault rifle more often.  These rifles, like their real world counterparts, should have a fire mode selection option and the ability to equip a silencer like the Ghost Recon series games do.

Lastly, one of the biggest negatives of all is the aggravating game save.  Saves are few and very far between.  You can be over an hour of slow painstaking maneuvering into the mission and have to leave for some reason (say for dinner) and nothing gets saved and you maddeningly have to start the whole mission over from the beginning.  We need way more frequent saves.  Nobody want to go all the way back to a very long mission and start from scratch.  It’s rage inducing.

On a positive note though, the graphics in the Kolchak Harbor campaign are simply stunning.  They’re mind blowing visually.  Some of the other locations are very elaborate and very well done.  I found myself ignoring the mission objectives at times and just looking around to take it all in.  I loved the water at Kolchak Harbor.

Because of the flaws at this time, I can’t recommend this game just yet, certainly not at full price.  If you can get it on sale,  then go ahead and buy it as it does have potential and I’m hoping the developer will address these issues in time.

The flaws I listed could easily be fixed and when they get addressed, I will give this game a enthusiastic  “yes” recommendation.

I'm on the fence about this one.

And I'm really, REALLY easily pleased, so me being on the fence means that for most people, it's a bad choice.

Contracts has some amazing things in it, like the bullet cam, and the sniper scope. The windage metres, the modifiers for distance that go up and down, etc, they all make the scope intuitive and so great for sniping. It's such a refreshing change from (even previous entries in this series as well as other sniping games) holding your breath and having a diamond show up showing you exactly where to aim. It's a beautiful innovative bridge between the worlds of just telling where the player where to aim, and giving them the tools to figure it out on their own. So instead of sitting down and trying to figure out where the bullet is going to land, you can instead focus on picking off targets and the order of killing, figuring out how to clear a base, etc. It's nice.

It's just a shame that almost everything else in the game is so very poorly executed.

Case in point. There are about six 'secondary weapons', and none of them can equip a suppressor. This game beats you over the head with stealth, and punishes you harshly for being discovered, and your assault rifles can't even equip suppressors.

They even have a SLOT for 'barrel' attachments. Just none of them actually have any attachments there. Like so much of this game, it feels [i]incomplete[/i]. It feels like a demo of a larger game, with all of the cool shit locked off. Except it never unlocks. You're just stuck with this.

The world is technically 'open'. But it's open like a Hitman game. Lots of small, interconnecting areas with very few ingress points. Objectives are 'randomized' in the most ephemeral of ways. A computer you need to hack might be in a different room, for instance.

The interface is... confusing. Confusing as fuck. And the maps are really rather small. Some parts are complex, but there really is just no reason to explore them. You can't find hidden resources for extra money, or hidden upgrades for your guns. Everything you have and can get is based around [i]money[/i], and the only way to get money is by completing objectives, looting bodies, or completing challenges. So any complexity in the map is immediately lost to the wind since there's no cool shit to find and gather while you're moving through the rooms.

The game page implies that there's this ever-changing world of contracts you can take. But there's not. Go and play a mission in Ghost Warrior 3, except move one of the secondary objectives to a room 15 metres away and that's about all the 'randomizing' you'll find in this. And even though you can tackle each 'objective' on a given map any way you want, it somehow stills feels incredibly linear. Your objectives for each map never change. They're static. And they'll force you to visit each main area of the map. There are some small side passages you can do 'for the funsies' but all you get out of it is looting 5 more bodies worth of money or whatever.

Your assault rifle (woefully unsuppressed for no good goddamn reason) is also inaccurate is fuck. You'll miss about 85% of shots beyond 50 metres away. Oh, and your 'contract killer for hire' in all the missions I've done so far, at least, has been killing 'morally repugnant' individuals. So even that bit from the main page was a lie. You might as well just be a peacekeeper or a vigilante, the whole 'mercenary' thing only seems to be shoehorned in to explain why you get money for capping the evil bad guys, and (very badly) explains why you have a cool high-tech sniping mask.

So in short, some decent ideas let down by horrific execution.

If they took this 'contracts' concept and made it actually randomized, used the maps from Ghost Warrior 4, scattered a wealth of collectables and unlockable gadgets and attachments and paintjobs and whatnot around the maps (maybe even having some of them locked behind difficult static contracts in between the random ones) and got rid of this juvenile 'I want to be a contract assassin BUT I WANNA BE THE GOOD GUY TOO' bullshit, then I would be EXCITED for that game. I'd suffer through the wonky controls to play it. And I would love it.

But that is not what this game is.

Wow. So, let's try and unpack a bit of this.

The story is not as bad as the second game, but it's definitely more forgettable and vapid. In the end, [spoiler]you get recruited by some vague, nameless group that's on par with the pop culture version of the Illuminati, who have global interests and control in mind.[/spoiler] The characters all hint at something, but in the end, it amounts to nothing, and you are told nothing. The final two "regions" (missions) drag on and are logically disconnected, requiring you to find a battered cardboard box in the middle of the map as "evidence", or wanting you to pick up a stack of papers and books among other debris for "evidence". This is fairly ironic, given how the last two levels in the game tell you to run through them, as both have time-based completion challenges.

The weapons and gadgets are okay-ish, as you never really need to change your weapon past the first or second upgrade, but this also makes the combat and selection feel pointless and shallow. The perks are yet again logically unsound and just gameified stat/abi bonuses rather than semi-logical upgrades. Hey, at least 1/3 of this game's weapons are not paid DLC/P2W, unlike its sequel.

And that kinda leads me to the conundrum: this game attempts to set up a realistic/surrealistic set and setting, but it fails miserably as there's no real justification for anything. Perks that make no sense, innate abilities that make no sense, required weapon purchases because your damage magically dissipates in later levels, characters that give you nothing or speak the obvious when interrogated. It's a shockingly valid example of making a game based on arbitrary mechanics and definitions rather than its own established universe and drive.

Finally, for the Sniper Elite comparisons. Yes, I still stand by what I said for my review of the second game, where if the general concept of these games were done well, it could beat any given Sniper Elite title at its own game. However, this is not done well, let alone to perfection, and the two are quite different anyways. The only similarities are that they're both allegedly based on sniping, and this game shamelessly implements a bullet camera effect that's just as fairly repetitive as Sniper Elite's. Beyond that, eh, more Ghost Warrior.

I am very glad that I spent less than $10 on the pack, as I could not reasonably justify spending any more on it. Given what it is that I did per-mission, I would say that it was worth $1/hour.

I recently finished this game but being honest I found it frustrating in several ways. 

As a plus, the graphics in the game look great - very detailed, scroll smoothly and obviously a lot of work has gone into the environments you move around in. 

However, I found quite a few disappointing things about this game:

- A manual save option is badly needed as having to backtrack to a known save point (sometimes a very long distance) is frustrating and time wasting. I also found that when you log in to play again after saving, quite often you are not in the same location you were in when you saved the game, not always but quite often 

- The reactions of the opponents is very poor. I found several times that you can walk up right beside an enemy before they become aware of you and sometimes not even then. I also found at times that they show no response to a soldier killed right beside them 

- I see some people saying they hated the aiming and firing process used in the game. It does take a bit of getting used to but once mastered, it is easy to use 

- When checking an area to tag enemies, I sometimes found that they just vanish as you are watching them and also sometimes they (for some reason) drop down to the bottom of the screen and vanish from play 

- There was a glitch with the health setting. I had been hit badly by enemy fire and had virtually no life left. As I fled, I stumbled over a high ledge and was sure I would be dead. However, when I hit the ground my health restored to 100% and stayed that way for the rest of the level no matter how much damage I took 

- There was also a glitch with climbing. I jumped into the air from a height to reach a ledge but missed the ledge. However, instead of falling, I was standing in the air and the game allowed me to climb the ledge I had been aiming for even though I was not close to it 

- When approaching the dam on the final level, I approached from the valley with the train wreck in it. It was completely empty right to the end and I was able to watch and tag enemies. However, when I went to return there were about a dozen enemies that I encountered and killed. They were meant to be there the entire time but when I first walked down the valley it was absolutely empty when they were actually meant to be there


Overall, this is a lovely looking game but it is badly let down by the issues I raised above and so I feel I couldn't recommend it. There is much more satisfaction, interaction and challenge to be had in the Sniper Elite games

I want this game to be fun, the main concept for a great game is here. Sadly, the amount of bugs, issues and design choices makes it so underwhelming. 

AI: Detection is all over the place, some enemies you can run right past without being detected, where as other enemies will detect you the moment you jump 30 meters away from them. Using any gadget will alert them, rendering all EMP related devices useless. Sometimes stealth killing an enemy could instantly alert the whole base because the body rag dolling somewhere off a ledge or simply due to the fact the enemy can spot dead bodies from further away than the player. When the player gets detected, even at actual long ranges the AI will instantly start to return fire. Heavy's spray in your detection and despite all the tracers missing you, the player still takes damage from some unknown source.

Weapons: The snipers in this game feel weak, there is a ton of bullet drop and wind compensation which I understand from a gameplay point of view. The majority of the time the easiest way to complete a zone is to snipe the HVT if there is one, and then use the AK to take out all the other soldiers. Damage is seemingly random, for the 7.62 rifles shooting a heavy solider in the neck can either instantly kill, or just do damage. There has not been a single case where I would've wanted to take out a .50 due to them not being able to accept suppressors. The fire rate on the semi 7.62 rifles is way to low, other bolt action rifles shoot almost just as fast. Besides that, I've never had a scenario where the usage of ammo types was relevant, a wasted opportunity. Bolting a rifle is way faster when still scoped in, un-scoping while still in the animation causes it to cancel out and requiring you to do another animation from start, this time way slower than what is possible scoped.

Optimization: This game has been highly optimized, meaning it runs really well, but at a draw back of not having enemies presist despite being able to technically shoot at them. This unloading prevents a lot of long range shots that would've been great to make. Bodies will de-spawn after leaving LOS from the player, or when a save is loaded.

Controller first: It is clear that the game was designed on a controller first environment. Keys and actions overlapping each other. Thermal and scanning are two modes bound to the same key. Using something, looting, swapping weapons and interrogating are all the same key too. Besides key issues, there are also quite a few mouse related quirks. Depending on your stance your sensitivity gets drastically changed, making it impossible to apply any muscle memory. Drones have a really aggressive sensitivity curve rather than it just being one single value. Camera sensitivity is terrible, as you can not change this with any sensitivity setting. 

Features: Some areas have a "Anti-tagging" radio tower. Which just feels terrible, it takes away all the upgrades for scanning you've worked towards and basically nullifies them. Some upgrades that are available are worthless, the final drone upgrade has a pathetic 10 meter range and chews through the battery. Where as some actively make the experience less enjoyable, like having to switch camo types if you go between a snowy level or a forested level. Bullet cam when activated has just a few different animations, even when set to the lowest frequency possible I saw the same animation multiple times to the point I simply just turned the feature off. 

DLC: They're worthless, skins or weapons, just don't get them. The only reason I got some was as they where included from the humble bundle where I got this game from.

Saving: Check points are thrown around seemingly arbitrarily, sometimes putting you right in front of an enemy when reloading a save causing the alarms to go off right away. A manual save and load button would've prevented all those issues.

Bugs: I've had times where I've experienced no fall damage when jumping off 5 stories, but I've also had times where jumping down from half a staircase I've instantly died. Saving and re-loading a save file will re-set the aggro status of enemies. Sometimes the "restart mission" and "Load last checkpoint" buttons grey out and you are unable to use them. The "Load last checkpoint" has a confirm dialog, even when the player has died. When the player has died, sometimes the "restart mission" button would be selected. Some areas which you should easily be able to crawl under will prevent you from doing so. Sounds sometimes wouldn't play, turrets are the biggest offender of these, going from undetected to instantly melting you in 1 second.

A majority of these issues could've been fixed by users if modding the game was supported. But with the release of the multiplayer update and the addition of EAC has basically ruined these chances. I want this game to be good, but sadly CI seems to not be interested in making good games, just good enough to get their money.

SGWC(1) was somewhat enjoyable at first.  It's like a mashup of Sniper Elite and parts of Far Cry Blood Dragon in a way.  But after playing thru it, I started discovering it's major flaws.  I would not waste my time playing thru it again.  The controls are poorly planned out, and are sometimes unresponsive.

-- I'll start with the most annoying thing.  You CANNOT adjust your position via the movement keys while in scope view.

You can change your stance, but you absolutely cannot move left/right (or forward/back) to adjust your shot.  That's just dumb.  If you need to adjust for objects in between you and the target, you can't.  You would have to leave scope view, adjust without being able to see, then go back into scope view to see if you adjusted enough.  By the time you get the right positioning, the target has moved on.  Major fail on that one devs.

-- Picking up a body and melee are the same control. (and the game does not prioritise melee over picking up.)

So if you are sneaking up on someone that was hiding, and his dead buddies are around him, your character would rather pick up a nearby body, getting spotted by the target you were trying to sneak up on in the process, and you're dead because you can't use your weapons while holding a body,  This one just made me shake my head.  It's so stupid.

-- The challenges are set up in a way that forces you to do multiple playthroughs.

Meaning, some of the challenges contradict each other.  No need for examples.  I'm pretty sure you know what I mean.

-- Some seriously bad hitboxes on the final map/mission.  (The one the devs should have put the most time into.)

I lost count of the number of times I had a perfect shot, especially someone standing in the open, and my shot would be deflected off of an invisible hitbox from an object 3 feet away.  I got so frustrated with the last mission, I didn't even worry about the challenges.

All I can say in conclusion is that I hope SGWC2 is way better than this.  The SGW series is, after all, the same game as Sniper Elite. (same menu format, same interface, same HUD/interface sounds offset in tone, etc.) i.e. SGWC is based off of SE3, although I enjoyed SE3 immensely.  And supposedly SGWC2 is based off of SE4.  We'll see.

I've been trying to give this game the best possible chance to impress me and I, frankly, can't give it a positive rating for a few things that really should be minor but aren't. That said, I *really* like the way this game works, most of the time. It takes most of the annoyances I had with similar games and throws them out.

That said, the minor things tend to add up. I often find I have issues with the placements of enemy spotters and rival bounty hunters. There's this one map where a sniper spotter, for the enemy, is placed waaaaaay out of bounds on a ship with a bunch of shipping crates. I was looking around for him for several minutes because I, quite reasonably, assumed that the spotter would be on the actual world map I was playing on, and not in the background where things usually don't even have collision detection. There are a few other placements that seem goofy as hell, where they're on rooves that have no reasonable way for anyone to get to.

And then there's the sentries. Later stages have them in spades and there's just no good way to deal with them. With the rifle I use, it takes eight shots to shut just one down. EMP grenades and ammo restocks aren't plentiful enough to account for all the sentries you deal with later on, and the range on those grenades is so ridiculously small you can only ever knock out one sentry at a time. Even if you do that, good luck doing so without blowing your cover, the blast radius is so small you have to be very accurate with your throw. I often find it more worth my time to just try and run past them.

And then there's the issue others have mentioned, where if you even slightly bork one shot, and don't immediately kill that person as soon as the next shot is ready, every enemy knows your location instantly. You can be prone in an area where the game recognizes you as fully hidden and you'll still be exposed. Meanwhile I can be shot by an enemy sniper and the recognition as to which direction I got shot from is so vague it's unhelpful beyond telling me which cardinal direction to look in.

And then there's the bounties. If you're not ready to tackle them, make SURE you don't enter the areas for them, because if you try to leave, the game will act like you died and reload you at the last checkpoint in the bounty area. You cannot leave until you kill the target.

But for positives, I like that you can use silenced secondary weapons and sidearms. I like that there are infinite marks you can use. I like the story explanation for unrealistic abilities (healing, surviving falls, aim assistance with wind/distance etc.) in an otherwise hyper-realistic game. I love the environments, with how beautiful and realistic they are. I like how the game gives you multiple ways to approach enemy strongholds so that you're not forced into a singular way to deal with them (great for replay value). I (mostly) like the way the AI works regarding their alert system. So much of the game is just on point that it's a pity the downsides bring it down.

[i] Its first-person Hitman. You have a large maps with large zones with hits or challenges to accomplish in each area, and a skill tree in a pre-game briefing screen. You can upgrade your sniper rifle, secondary, side-arm and gadgets as you finish hits and challenges as you earn credits for everything you complete. You can exfiltrate anytime you want during a mission at exfiltration points and upgrade your gear there and reload at these points with the same progress you had when you saved and quit at. [/i]

[h1] Nice things: [/h1]
[spoiler]
-1st Person Hitman format.
-Nice large and detailed maps. Open-world feel to linear mission-centered design. Like Crysis 1 tbh.
-Exfiltration zones for early upgrading after finishing hits/challenges. No need to finish whole level.
-Minimalistic interface(doesnt look lazy and unfitting. It looks Hitman 2 inspired. Beautiful.), briefing screen, ambient ominous wind gushes
-Suppressed and unsuppressed gun sounds
-Graphics are nice. Reflections. Shadows. Shaders. You know. Its modern and realistic... I had it all on very high but I turned some shadows down to save frames. It still looked fine to me. I'm not picky with graphics.
-Checkpoints and autosaves are consistent where you move to and after kills. If you kill someone after detection you DO have a window to pause and reload a checkpoint before sniping.
-The rangefinder is great.
-The different ammo types are good for taking on turrets, heavy juggernauts soldiers
[/spoiler]

[h1] My Issues: [/h1] 
[spoiler]
-Many X-Ray Vision perks. Hand-holdy perks. You arent hiding from the enemy cause you can see them from miles away. So this isnt a stealth game. End of story. (Its also a final perk)
-Tags (The bane of all stealth game mechanics. They should be locked to easy modes, but Normal? Hard? Veteran? Give us a hardcore experience. No tags. Easier detection. Same kind of weapon damage. Just narrower detection windows. THAT'S HOW IT SHOULD BE.)
-I uninstalled because I got all the perks I felt I needed. It felt too easy on level 4 since I took my time upgrading everything and doing all challenges.
-I think the old Hitman games did it better: No perks, Weapons and gear have more importance. Upgrading your stealth detection reduction stat... will just sound like its tied to difficulty. 
-Peak-a-boo stealth alarm meter is a joke now. 
(I remember playing Thief thinking this meter is an annoying mini-game but I did feel like an assassin hiding in the dark waiting to strike. In this game, I'm dueling with snipers that think they are spotting me. Reloading checkpoints is the mini-game with killing snipers)
-It has a Multiplayer. Which is dead. Since release in 2019. 
-Not enough levels. It has only 5 of them... 5.
-Takedowns and chain kills feel awkward. Not like Dishonored.

Pros:
Realistic Weaponry: The weapons are really well modeled and are based on real-world weapons
Realistic Bullet Physics: You have to compensate for both bullet drop, wind and even lead your shots on a moving target.
Satisfying "Killcams": They very much took a page out of Sniper Elite, giving you a sick slow-mo cinematic camera on your bullet flying directly towards your target's cranium or nutsack (No X-Ray).

Cons:

Don't come here expecting the most accurate experience. Sure, there's correct wind and gravity compensation, buut what training do these soldiers go through? Unless your character uses tracer bullets, I have no idea how these soldiers are able to see and perfectly shoot a camo mercenary from 300 meters away. Sure you can say "tHeY hAvE bInOcUlArS", but your merc (who, I must say, is a total fucking wuss since you can die instantly from falling higher than like 10 or 15 feet) has access to the most advanced technology available including "Advanced Camo".

They say this game is in "Sandbox Worlds", but there's [b]COUNTLESS[/b] invisible walls that restrict you from getting incredible vantage points that could put the odds in your favor immensely. Not to mention, if the ledge you're trying to grab doesn't have a piece of paracord next to it, it's impossible to climb unless you're able to jump high enough.

Each and every level is against you. No matter what, you are guaranteed to get detected once. Out of the 4/5 worlds that I've played in, I've been detected each and every time. 

There's these "Side Contracts" you can do, and you faiil them automatically if you leave the contract area. This wouldn't be an issue [b]if they ever showed you what the contract area is[/b]. There's no blue line, no border area, not even an outline on the map.

Half of the upgrades for your character don't even work or change anything, just placebo effects. The Camo upgrades do nothing at all, still detected within 1.5 seconds of a camera or person seeing me, even in bushes. "Drone Towers" are like Jammers, but for your drones, and are on nearly [b]every map[/b], they're indestructible as well so Drones are pretty much pointless. The "Wraith" upgrade is supposed to make your character silent when walking or running, but enemies still hear you as if you didn't have the upgrade, the devs just remove the walk/running noises. Not to mention, the "chain attack" upgrade only works when the guards are quite literally shoulder-to-shoulder, if they're ~4 feet away from you then good luck. This wouldn't be too bad if they couldn't [b]still kill you while in the chain attack cutscenes[/b].

Nearly every challenge is nigh impossible.

There is supposed to be "creativity" and "open-endedness" to your approaches, but this is just as creativity-stifling as Fallout 76. There [i]is no creativity[/i]. Your options are:
1. Shoot, get spotted by binoculars, sneak around to another side/distract with a drone (if there's no tower, which there probably is), rinse and repeat until the whole complex is empty.
2. Guns blazing, die because of a heavy being nigh-indestructible without AP/heavy bullets, restart, snipe the heavy you died to last time, and continue.
3. Metal Gear Solid.

There are glaring issues that the devs could easily fix, but no. They want you to suffer.

So after 19 hours I'm ready to draw a conclusion - also because the game really annoys me with some game mechanics. In this review there might be some Spoilers so beware. Conclusion at the bottom.

[b] Graphics: [/b]
First of all - the game is all in all nice to look at, because it is based on the CryEngine. You have several graphics options etc. There is also a FoV slider - which is not always guaranteed nowadays.

[b] Story: [/b]
It's about a fictitious republic in Russia, more precisely the Republic of Siberia. After an uprising and a fight for independence, this republic is now autonomous, albeit by force of arms.
One is assigned as a sniper to kill important members of the said republic and to reveal their researches / secrets.

[b] Gameplay: [/b]
Let's get to the point that will last the longest.
This is a sniper game - you kill 90% of all targets or enemies with your sniper rifle, you have to take into account the distance and the wind speed (the game gives you help even on the highest difficulty level). This help is provided by a mask that you receive from your client at the beginning of the game. This mask has some useful functions, like detecting enemies, mines, weak points of vehicles and as already mentioned it helps with sniping. Also as mentioned before there are different levels of difficulty - in this case three of them. You are able to purchase different Snipers, Pistols and Assault Rifles. All of your guns can be customized aswell with Silencers, muzzle brakes, differenz Scopes, Ammuniton and of course Camouflages.

Let's get to the points that are annoying. It can happen that at some points in the game you fall through the map and have to reload it. There are times where your character or NPCs are having trouble walking some paths and sliding down some slobs is not really fun. At some terrain points it seems to me as if our "professional sniper" is the greatest amateur there is, he can't even climb a bigger rock without problems and move around there, no you have to keep on jumping like a fool to get one little jump further up. Most of the time when it comes to this point you will be seen or almost seen by opponents which is of course annoying.
The AI in this game is a bit split in two, in some moments the AI is not able to think at all - the next moment the AI is as smart as a supercomputer. You can snipe away enemies one by one without anyone noticing, but if you miss twice, EVERY enemy in the area knows where you are AUTOMATICALLY via TELEPATHY. If you can still kill the enemy fast enough, nothing happens, but if you wait about 2 seconds too long, you have to reload the checkpoint. Of course the enemies can also spot you trough objects and terrian, also the kilometer wide shooting with assault rifles (and hitting) is included. In some moments it is really easier to just kill all the enemies in the area (no matter if someone has been alerted), because as soon as you go to another area nobody knows what happened in the other area. Even if you work with mines, hand grenades and C4 or shoot your way out with an assault rifle, in my eyes a bit strange.
In every mission there are main tasks that have to be done and also "Challanges" these are completely optional. Unfortunately some of them do not fit into a sniper game at all. For example - kill enemies with hand grenades or mines, blind enemies with flash bangs etc. I find it a little bit incomprehensible what such tasks are doing there, I am there as a sniper to (actually) only kill my target and not to start the third world war.
The missions usually last between 25 minutes (if you already know where to go) and about 1 hour+ if you want to be extremely stealthy or your just not getting lucky. For the missions – you have 5 Missions and a Trainings Mission.

[b] Conclusion: [/b]
I think the game is not bad, but unfortunately there are so many little things that are simply not solved well (e.g. telepathic communication between the enemies).
I can recommend this game if you just want to have some action and don't mind taking out all the enemies instead of sneaking through.  On the other hand, if you want to play the missions the way they are supposed to be played, it becomes very difficult to recommend it..
