PROS:
--Sniping and level design are way more refined and polished compared to 3

--No more open world, so the graphics are improved immensely thanks to more focused priorities

--Runs so much smoother than 3 that you'll think 3 and Contracts were developed by two different companies 

--Gameplay loop is more akin to Hitman than anything, which does wonders

--First person platforming and climbing were done remarkably well, almost on par with games like Mirror's Edge.  

CONS: 
-- buggy as hell. Devs have done a great job with the patches so far, but when I was playing it, I would get stuck in certain parts of the map, get stuck cold-turkey when trying to sprint over ankle-high elevation, hitched reloading animations, etc.  Not sure if any of this has been fixed satisfactorily or not, your mileage may vary, etc 

--Story is nonexistent compared to 3 (maybe this is a PRO for you?)  As someone who actually enjoyed the most story-oriented 3, this was a CON for me.  Very little interaction between characters, and the ending is unsatisfying as hell, which seems to be a pattern with these games.

--Once you complete the maps, there is very little to call you back to the game

--Guns range from completely worthless to overpowered as hell. (don't even bother with shotguns, you will get destroyed)

--Assault Rifles are unwieldy and have way more kickback than you'd initially think, but then, I'm playing with a gamepad, so what do I know with my heretic ways?

--The Desert Eagle seem to be bugged, as it is the only weapon without vibration feedback. EDIT: KELL-T SHOTGUN WAS FIXED, NOW HAS VIBRATION

-- Mask HUD mechanics are poorly executed, making stealth an exercise in frustration.  Hard to detect enemies before they detect you, especially enemy snipers. Trying to stay out of combat is just a massive pain, as enemies have that oft-dreaded "telepathy." (You get spotted by a lone guard, expect the entire map to be on your ass in an instant) 

--Terrible auto save system that sets you back way too much when you get killed (no manual saving).   

Underneath the bugs, imbalances, and poorly executed stealth, there is a winning formula here. This game probably has more potential than it does quality at this time.  But considering it's, in a way, better and worse simultaneously than SGW 3....And is only 30 dollars, I give this game a hesitant thumb sideways.

It seems like the developers have learned from their previous mistake, at least somewhat. While the game still features an open world design with five maps to explore, it now no longer invokes Far Cry as much anymore by having you endlessly drive around the place and fill the map with tons of pointless markers. The sniping gameplay, the core around which everything else is built is better than ever. As before, you need to take wind, bullet drop off and even the travel time of your bullets into consideration. This can obviously be a bit of a challenge if you don’t have an intuitive way of knowing where a bullet is going to land once you fire it. 

Contracts actually has a neat little twist in the way it provides aim assist to you, in that it doesn’t give you the exact point the bullet will hit, instead just showing a general drop off curve along which the bullet will travel. I like that this increases the skill floor from the previous game somewhat but keeps it accessible to newcomers. However, the previous games allowed you to turn this aim assist feature off entirely and the hardest difficulty didn’t even allow using it, which you can no longer do. And even while I wouldn’t have turned it off myself, reducing options for players is always worthy of criticism. 

So if the sniping gameplay is better than ever and some of the faults of the previous ones haven’t made a return, this game must be quite good, right? Well, unfortunately not. 

For one, even though the maps are no longer typical sandboxes, they’re still incredibly annoying to navigate. Usually, you have three or four places on each map that house objectives, but enemies are present even outside of them, so walking around from place to place makes no sense for the most part if you can just bypass everyone with the fast travel system. But even fast travel is implemented in a fairly shoddy manner. I’ve had it happen multiple times that enemies spawned within meters of my own location upon loading the section of map and even when starting a level, which is incredibly annoying. 

Thankfully, most of the time, the enemies were entirely unaware of my presence. That isn’t to say that enemies don’t still exhibit the infuriating ability of spotting you halfway across the map whenever so much as one of your bum cheeks sticks out of cover. It’s just that enemies behave entirely unpredictably here. It’s almost as if the game decides at random whenever it gives the enemies super vision, so progression through these levels can really end up testing your patience. And it’s not like you don’t already need to bring buckets worth of patience to begin with, since whenever enemies are alerted to your presence, they immediately hunker down and refuse to move even an inch and the game takes an eternity to reset them to an unalerted status, even if you leave the area entirely. 

I’m overall not a big fan of how the actual mission sites are designed either. Contracts usually give you two targets to kill per map, while the other objectives revolve around retrieving something from somewhere or planting explosives. Can you tell where those two ideas conflict with each other already? That’s right, we’re playing a sniping game, so the thing players want from that is shooting enemies from as far away as humanly possible. As in, not even setting foot into an enemy compound if at all possible. Not that that’s even doable, since most of the time, the compounds are located between mountainous terrain or other hindrances that the game for some reason refuses to let you climb over. You only get to climb up ropes, ladders and ledges that are clearly defined by the game, there’s absolutely no freeform way of approaching these levels. You’ll have to do it exactly as the developers intended. 

Having to retrieve something from somewhere or planting explosives means you actually have to infiltrate every single compound on the map, meaning that Contracts wants to be a stealth game as well. But again, enemy visibility is so arbitrary that this is already a losing proposition. And given that I personally was there for the sniping gameplay, I mostly accomplished all the goals by methodically taking out enemies and the actual targets from afar, strolling into the compound without any resistance and gathering whatever needed picking up with no enemies in sight. Why would I pick up a game called Sniper Ghost Warrior and do something other than sniping? That’s what I’m here for, but the game tries as hard as possible to make it about anything but sniping. 

Take for example the challenges you can do in each level, like it’s a fu[i][/i]cking Hitman game or something. Each map gives you a bunch of additional challenges to complete, from killing the targets in a predetermined time limit to doing the entire mission with just your knife. That last one is actually given in the same map that also has another entirely different challenge of killing an enemy from over 300m distance, as if the game wants to brag about all the replay value it has. 

If you’ve paid attention, I mentioned that not all of Far Cry’s habits have returned here. And I also mentioned enemy tagging a few paragraphs ago. So yes, just like in the Far Cry games, most of the time you’ll start every infiltration by keeping a lookout for all the enemies and tagging them on your HUD. And I have to ask, why can we only tag enemies with the binoculars and not directly with the sniper scope? It’s just pointless busywork to switch between the two every single time you notice an enemy you haven’t tagged yet while scoping. But that’s not enough in the way of finally getting to the shooting. As mentioned before, the game also features certain compounds with jamming equipment that disable tagging entirely and prohibit the use of the drone. I don’t care that it’s realistic for someone to set up an anti-drone perimeter, it’s just not fun. 

Speaking of realism, the game also wants you to exfiltrate every single site after completing the objective. It doesn’t matter that in my case, most of the time I had disposed of every single enemy in the compound before I got to the point where I needed to pick up something. I still had to walk out of the place in order to get to the designated exfiltration spot. And why did I have to go to those spots to just upload some data? Seriously, why do I even have to do that? I have a constant connection with my handler, why can’t I just upload the data from wherever I am and just move on to the next part? This entire rigmarole is only there because this Contracts wants to be a stealth game. But it just isn’t a good stealth game, it’s moveset and gameplay are too static and contextual to provide the necessary freedom for emergent gameplay and its levels are designed in ways that don’t incentivize stealth. Especially given the fact that you have a god[i][/i]damn sniper rifle at your disposal, so dealing with enemies from a distance is not only what most players who pick up a game called Sniper Fu[i][/i]cking Ghost Warrior show up for, it’s a preferable alternative to trying to infiltrate these compounds unseen.

It’s a shame that CI Games simply can’t manage to knock out a good game in this series. They’ve tried so hard and it’s sad to see that the competent sniping gameplay is once again wasted beneath layers of forced stealth gameplay, schizophrenic enemy AI, highly funneled level design that disincentivizes clever traversal and non-existent writing. Heck, even the one thing the previous game excelled at isn’t around anymore and that’s the music. So in essence, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts is another sub-par entry in this series and as such, I can’t really recommend it to anyone but the most hardcore fans of sniping gameplay.

For the pro's, everything in this game works. The wind and range systems are neat, the UI is clean and easy to use, watching your shots land feels satisfying. Unfortunately, the awful enemy AI and zero interesting objectives make playing a repetitive and uninteresting experience.

Enemy alerts in this game are global, meaning that when one enemy is alerted, all enemies in the area will suddenly know exactly where you are. This does not combo well with the instant-kill snipers, or full auto enemies, who have almost perfect accuracy regardless of your range from them. This creates a frustrating loop where you will often be shot down from across the map by enemies who had no realistic way of knowing your position.

This combined with the lack of interesting enemies, completely broken ledge grab system, pointless and annoying exfil system, lack of manual saves, useless gadgets, and cookie cutter story make this game feel outright rushed to completion. The bones of a good game are here, and if on heavy sale it's probably still worth buying, but overall SGWC is an unimpressive mess of a sniper game that feels clunky in every aspect.

I love sniper games.  I find them to be very stress relieving.  Stalking through the bushes carefully dispatching bad dudes with well placed digital lead can be very cathartic.  So, I wish I loved this entry in the SGW chapter, but I didn't.  I didn't hate it, but I think it is overall a big step backwards from its predecessor.

The pros: Sniping mechanics themselves are great imo, especially at higher difficulties, though it drives me crazy that I can't tag people through the scope, I have to use the binoculars to do it first.  This is supposed to add some level of 'realism' I guess, but its just extra steps.  But bullet drop, variable wind and bullet impact is all there, and it is satisfying to plan out your attack depending on your play style.  You can remain that ghost warrior and pick your way through enemies from afar trying not to raise suspicion, or you can go in and try to strangle everyone, or you can go in like rambo and shoot up the place.  Keep in mind that you're still a meat sponge and it doesn't take all that much to kill you, so your mileage may vary.

The graphics and environments are beautiful, and it all ran smoothly for me with my 5700XT at a 21:9 1440p, though I did experience spots here and there with an inexplicable stutter in performance.  

Negs: Well, SGW:Contracts is a bunch of, well, contracts.  They're a bunch of loosely tied together missions that reward you at the end with kind of a lame cutscene once you've completed everything.  I think its supposed to be some big aha moment, but it doesn't work.  I much enjoyed the story and atmosphere of the previous game much more.  You had a hideout! You could store and display your stuff! You could rest, or drive around the map looking for trouble and there was a day night cycle.  It was much more story based and immersive.  Contracts just feels disconnected, and that is really the least of its problems.  

Biggest problem for me is how limited you are by the maps and contract system.  Because each contract area is defined, you aren't totally free to find a perch or go your own way.  You're only able to climb up things they've designated (if you can get the damn controls to cooperate with you - which as an aside - movement in this game when you're trying to be athletic is clunky af.  Can't tell you how many times I just fell 50 feet for no damn reason), and this being a sniping game, I found it really hard to find really long shots. Heck, some of the optics range out to 500m but you'd be hard-pressed to find shots at 400m.  At least I couldn't. Most of my sniping seeming to take place between 100-200m.  I was able to get much longer shots out of Sniper Elite and that is set in WW2 with inferior equipment.  Also, once you're in this contract, you lose all sense of what you're trying to do.  The map is vague - you have a list of objectives, but nothing more than blue boxes indicating you should do something there.  Just kill everyone and eventually you'll succeed. 

Which leads me to UI/UX which is pretty abysmal.  Want to know what that 125,000 dollar sniper rifle does? Can it take heavy ammo? Can you add a suppressor? Will it blend a margarita? Well you have to buy it first to see that stuff.  Have you been playing for a couple of hours and have carefully picked through an amazing route to your objective, but the kitchen caught fire and you have to leave?  NO saving.  You'll start from a random checkpoint an hour before because we said so.  Just have one target or objective left in that contract? Too bad, you're still going to listen to and watch the details about the whole thing about 200 more times because that is our loading screen.  Hey, bullet cam is kinda neat the first 900 times, but its getting tedious.  Let me turn down the frequency.  Huh, that does nothing.  Also, when it kicks in, you completely lose your ability to make a follow on shot, so just turn it off.

The mask tech is supposedly the new hotness, but it is mostly gimmicky, and the key mapping to turn if on/off is the same as thermal vision.  I changed this mapping, but about 25% of the time, I turn on thermal vision anyway.  Which is particularly useless FYI. Kind of like most of the gadgets you buy in game. In general, you will be perfectly equipped for everything by like the second contract.  You need a slightly higher powered rifle and a couple of accessories.  50 cals are just loud, slow and pointless. Even things like the various grenade types are frustrating to use.  Apparently, once your throw is more than 10m from you, you no longer have a clue where it will land.  The target icon (which itself just blends in with the ground) just vanishes. It's like playing cornhole with a blindfold on.

Lastly, game length.  I put 25 very slow hours into this game. I'm a slow player in general and this seemed short to me.  I didn't 100% anything because the only way to do that is to complete silly achievements like 'gas 10 enemies' or 'troll 20 people on twitter'.  I'm not interested in playing the same map over and over a different way just to be a completionist.  So the game feels sort of phoned in from a content perspective.  

So in all, it has some fun parts, so it can be worth it at a good sale price, but don't go paying more than $10. It's a $10 game.

This game and it successor "Contracts 2" both suffer from game play defects. Most note worthy is the inability to transition from prone to crouch to stand from the prone position. The player is often left stuck prone from which there is no escape: often the character is frozen in place, leaving no option but to restart the mission; or in order to stand and run must crawl for 10m at which point you are killed. Other anomalies include bad contrast in the rifle scope view. The cross hairs are black and fade easily into the background leaving the player searching for them. In "Contacts" the enemy tag distance is in light red....very hard to see. There is also a quirk with the wind correction line in the scope (Contracts) that when the character holds his breath for a shot the correction line moves left requiring readjustment before the breath expires. Both games are deficient in the ability to resume from a point without having to replay the entire mission; contracts 2 gives an option to select a previous save to restart from at least, something the predecessor does not allow. 
There seems to be something about "game designer syndrome" that persists in most all games. It has to do with circa 1960 arcade games; where you loose and game over (for 25 cents!). Even exceptions there let you end the game with a score and you replayed if you chose to better it. It is unfathomable that a game today would be designed to have the player continually loose and have to replay the entire episode over and over ad nauseam. That aspect is the biggest gripe of players (older than 16) who just spent hours playing an episode. One of the other most frustrating things designers do is spawn enemies; particularly where there was none before; like right behind the player's character....surprise! "Sniper contracts" is full of this, plus not being able to escape being hit by enemy fire even when 300m away and behind a building or wall. Here again all for the propensity to have the player be defeated and have to play over. Somehow the thinking is that loosing depicts the difficulty of winning...duh! So if you don't care about any of this, then both games are for you. Good luck and enjoy!

--Terrain--
The terrain is fucking terrible. I find myself usually crouch-walking and prone-peeking angles and even the flattest, most innocuous-looking terrain will get the character stuck with no way out (except, by dropping a 'nade on your feet to kill yourself and choose to be booted to the last checkpoint, which, you have no control over, btw). The missions' environment and side objectives encourage you to play stealthily. Playing stealthily means crouch-walking most of the time. And with the navigation mesh as fucked up as it is, this takes the player out of the immersion and gives them a horrible experience.

--Respawn points--
When you force yourself to get to a save point, and then quit the game to finally do some irl stuff, when you return, you get placed to a default location of that save point region. Here I'm thinking I'll have a tactical advantage in this area that I know the game saved for me, yet, when I returned, I am placed somewhere else. WTF was that about?

Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts was released in 2019.
It is the fourth installment in the SGW franchise.

You play as a contract sniper assassin named "Seeker", 
under orders from "Handler", part of an unknown organization.
You'll have to carry out targeted assassinations and secondary objectives, 
to bring down the regime of the Siberian Republic.

You have a high-tech mask that you can use as binoculars, allowing you to mark enemies, 
and scan for surfaces to grab onto and objects to pick up.
The arsenal is quite varied, the shooting sensations are nice, and sniper shots trigger a Bullet Cam like in Sniper Elite.
The game is quite beautiful, thanks to the CryEngine. The scenery is snowy, beaten by the blizzard and topped by the northern lights.
Those are the only positive points I have to say about this game.

SGWC is riddled with stupid ideas that detract from the game.
The water is icy cold, and you'd better not venture into it for too long or you'll die of hypothermia.
The level design is as bad as it gets, with every conceivable, if not unimaginable, flaw.
The maps are immense, but there are no drivable vehicles!
Fast travel doesn't work after completing an objective!
Checkpoints are horribly misplaced, and the game doesn't save automatically when an objective is completed.
This is supposed to be an stealth game, but there are ultra-armored enemies where you need to go, making combat inevitable.
The ballistics are quite difficult to manage, especially as the enemies aim very well with any weapon, even at long range!
Maps are infested with minefields and robotic turrets that aimbot shamelessly.
Objectives are poorly marked on the map, which is virtually illegible.
You get fall damage for ridiculous jumps, as if you had the brittle bone disease... 
A pixelated pattern is displayed when you're shot, making the action blurred.

Get away from Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts while you can!
This dreck is staggeringly mediocre and a real pain to play.
Don't waste your money, buy the first two games in the series instead.
Otherwise, go for Sniper Elite, which is a TPS in more or less the same genre,

Let's face it, I'm going to finish the game, so I will keep playing it, but I really can't recommend it as a fun time. 

At it's basic level, Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts is the same game as most other similar sniping games.  You creep around a map throwing things at walls to tempt people over, kill them in stealth, then move on to the next person and repeat until you've either killed everyone, or enough to complete the level and save the hostages, or collect the items you were sent for.     

You play to earn money for your character and obtain upgrade rewards to get 'better' weapons and add attachments and gadgets to help improve your performance and to make things easier on yourself.   Be that a silencer, zoom, drone or similar.

I should love the game, but the number of bugs and issues are just too much to make it more annoying than fun.   Firstly, it suffers from the same issue that most of these types of games suffer from - you get seen, or someone finds a dead body, enemies all hide and are really alert for 5 minutes, then go back to business and forget that anything ever happened!      People are able to see you through walls, snipers can see you through walls that you can't see them through.  You can get stuck in trees unable to move (usually due to trying to do a takedown on someone and your character model jumping to their location), people can warp - you see them in one location, them instantly they are somewhere else!    Crashes to desktops, invisible walls, being in the water swimming and being unable to climb out onto the smallest of ledges!  Being unable to take someone down because they are on a tiny ledge a few centimetres high!!!   (EDIT: also want to add in the really helpful stealth mechanic of not being able to crouch crawl downstairs and getting stuck on the ledge, meaning you have to either walk away and walk back or jump... and the best getting stuck standing in a doorway so you have to restart your checkpoint!)

The list of bugs just go on and on and on and they really ruin the fun.   

There is no save system, you get ONE checkpoint that you get put back to if you die.  But note that if you die, you MAY get re spawned in the path of enemies that you originally snuck past, so your save is ruined and you need to start from scratch on that entire level.    There are only a handful of maps, all with several objectives and you will have to play them over and over to get all the objectives, to upgrade all your guns, etc. 

In the end, I really wanted to like the game, but the bugs really make it un-enjoyable.   I only have it because it came from a Humble Bundle, I really do think it would have been a refunded item if it had been bought from the store!   :(

Full of bugs.

You can simply be walking over a tiny crack or a bit of rubble and suddenly your character can't move. So when you're trying to collect a challenge like doing all the contracts without loading a checkpoint, the biggest threat is not the enemy soldiers, but hoping that you don't walk over the wrong spot. If you do, you've instantly failed the challenge because you can't do anything without reloading.

You can hack turrets and cameras to disable them, but there have been multiple times where I start getting targeted by a turret that I disabled 15 seconds earlier, or by cameras that I hacked. Reloading a checkpoint resets the status of any hacked cameras, even if the last checkpoint happened afterwards. 

Certain areas have boundaries where enemies don't show up until you officially enter the area, so you can be walking along into an area that looks absolutely clear (and targeting hasn't picked up anything), and a moment later, soldiers simply teleport into place 10 feet from you.

Sometimes you're required to loot the bodies of certain targets, but the game will happily "clean up" EVERY body if you move too far away. Bearing in mind that this is a game about sniping from a distance, it can be a normal event for you to hit a target from a distance and then temporarily leave the area. Seems like the game should at least tag certain bodies as "important" so they aren't removed.

Some challenges are worded pretty awkwardly - am I supposed to kill 2 targets within 8 minutes of starting the mission or 8 minutes between each other? Who knows? A challenge that says you can only use a knife will also allow you to use a silenced pistol to shoot a lock, and a grenade to open a door.

It has its fun moments but the bugs make it a really frustrating game to play.
Just get a Sniper Elite game
